## Independent review — REQUEST CHANGES (1 P1, 2 P2)

**Exact reviewed revision:** `7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926` against main at `a769e3041978a61cf75c6028c19407a3361cb77c` (compare shows 2 commits ahead, no commits behind; 11 changed files). **Owning issue:** [#1071](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/issues/1071). **Consumer:** [heylolo-evidence #33](https://github.com/Wladefant/heylolo-evidence/pull/33), accepted head `bb9adecf7a5077a0919b105bcd0e87c87736acc9` (merged).

**Summary:** The guarded wire envelope, tuple validation, per-spawn generation increment, retained generation, broker `list` capability, and stale-generation checks in `wait`/`send`/`stop`/`restart` are real and mostly coherent. A baseline parser rejects the new `guarded` opcode rather than silently executing unguarded controls. However, broker retirement can still result in side effects after its retiring notice and replay of the same guarded operation; a new `send` serialization creates a readiness deadlock-until-timeout; and rejected guarded stop/restart calls silently cancel their unrelated exit watcher. These are blockers for the requested producer and operation-atomicity guarantees. Do **not** merge as approved at this head.

### Finding 1 — [P1] Retirement notice is sent while accepted, possibly side-effecting operations remain in flight

**Files:** [broker.ts:608–625](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L608-L625), [broker.ts:520–558](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L520-L558), [broker.ts:1407–1450](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L1407-L1450), [client.ts:308–365](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/client.ts#L308-L365).

**Breaking interleaving:**
1. An authenticated guarded `send` with `signal: "SIGHUP"` targets a detached daemon whose persisted `{id,generation}` is current. `#handleLine` passes its single `#shuttingDown` check, then dispatch awaits record lookup / detached-output refresh.
2. Broker shutdown begins during that await. `shutdown()` sets `#shuttingDown = true` and immediately broadcasts `broker-retiring`, but does **not** drain `#inFlight` or cancel/await already-dispatched side-effecting operations. Detached processes are deliberately left running.
3. The old `#send` resumes and checks only id, generation, and record membership—not retirement. It can execute `root.killTree(SIGHUP)` **after the retirement notice**. If stdin was written before the notice but its flush was pending, the same acknowledgment ambiguity exists for written data.
4. The client treats every pending request as unanswered, discards the old socket on `broker-retiring`, and replays its exact wire line to the replacement broker. The replacement can recover that same detached `{id,generation}` and deliver a **second** SIGHUP. The guard cannot deduplicate a request against the *same* incarnation.

**Impact:** This violates the claimed fail-closed retirement and operation atomicity; guarded identity is not an exactly-once or broker-authority fence. Old brokers can act after stating that pending requests were not acted on. An operator signal may therefore execute twice on the same detached process; `stop`/`restart` operations have analogous uncontrolled post-await retirement windows. This matters independently of whether the race predated this diff: the required acceptance criterion is still unmet at the reviewed head.

**Required correction:** Establish an explicit retirement barrier for accepted requests and serialize acknowledgment/commit of side effects relative to retiring notices. Do not automatically replay ambiguous, potentially already-executed non-idempotent controls without deduplication or a proven no-side-effect rejection. Recheck broker authority after awaits and just before committing operations, while also handling actions that began before retirement. Add a deterministic test holding a detached guarded `send` at an asynchronous boundary, initiating broker retirement, and checking **one** signal/zero post-retirement side effects and no silent replay.

### Finding 2 — [P2] Newly serialized send cannot satisfy readiness while start is waiting

**Files:** [broker.ts:657–679](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L657-L679), [broker.ts:702–710](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L702-L710), [broker.ts:1564–1574](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/launch/broker.ts#L1564-L1574).

**Breaking sequence:** Start a daemon with `ready.log = "READY"` and `ready.timeoutMs = 30000`; its child prints `READY` only after receiving `go\n` on stdin. `#start` holds the name's `#serialized` lifecycle chain for its whole readiness wait. A second client can `list` and observe the already-admitted daemon's id/generation, then issue a **matching guarded send** of `go\n`. But this PR changes `send` from direct dispatch to `#serialized(name, ...)`, so that input is stuck behind the unresolved `start`. Readiness cannot occur until `start` times out (~30 s), after which the queued send finally runs. Previously `send` could supply input during the readiness wait.

**Required correction:** Keep serialization around the incarnation-changing admission/start commit and send's identity-checked I/O, **not** the entire asynchronous readiness wait; or otherwise allow a safe matching-generation send to proceed while readiness is pending. Regression test: start awaiting an stdin-generated banner, observe identity via `list`, send with the guard, and assert start returns ready before its deadline.

### Finding 3 — [P2] A rejected guarded stop/restart cancels a live daemon's exit-watch job

**Files:** [launch.ts:511–523](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/shell/launch.ts#L511-L523), [launch-exit-watch.ts:86–110](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/shell/launch-exit-watch.ts#L86-L110), [launch-exit-watch.ts:144–151](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/blob/7ff96c2aba5f87d2caecc7c3f688b8ad4bff7926/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/shell/launch-exit-watch.ts#L144-L151).

**Breaking sequence:** Start a non-detached daemon and allow `watchLaunchedProcessExit` to register its background completion job. Then call the tool with `op: "stop"` or `"restart"`, the same name but a **wrong or outdated `{expectedId,expectedGeneration}`** (even an invalid generation rejected locally works). `LaunchTool.execute` calls `releaseLaunchExitWatch(...)` **before** `operationFor` validation or `client.request` confirmation. The broker correctly rejects the stale guard; the process survives, but the exit-watch has already been canceled, so a later natural failure/exit never reports to the initiating session. This introduces a tool-visible side effect on a guard rejection.

**Required correction:** Build/validate the operation before changing watches, and cancel only once the intended incarnation's stop/restart has been accepted, or reliably restore the watch on rejection. Track watcher identity, not just `${projectDir}+name`. Add tests for rejected guarded stop/restart preserving the original background exit notice.

### Contract and source review by changed file

| Changed file | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| `src/launch/protocol.ts` | Complete guard pair validation and `guarded` envelope; parses generation and `list.capabilities.guardedIdentity: 1`; ordinary wire operations with stray guard fields reject. |
| `src/launch/client.ts` | Correctly encodes a guarded request before socket transmission; retirement retransmission remains unsafe for ambiguous already-executed effects (Finding 1). |
| `src/launch/broker.ts` | Id+generation+live-record checks; post-flush recheck and pinned `input`/`pty`/native root; generation advanced per `#launch` and captured in completion/recovery. Retirement barrier and send-readiness issues remain (Findings 1–2). |
| `src/launch/completions.ts` | Intentional schema bump 2→3; version mismatch discards old retained history instead of mis-parsing it. |
| `src/tools/shell/launch.ts` | Guard fields accepted for only wait/send/stop/restart; details propagate capabilities; watcher canceled prior to validation/execution (Finding 3). |
| `test/fixtures/launch-base-wire-parser.ts` | Models old unknown-op rejection; consistent with base protocol behavior. |
| `test/launch/guarded-protocol.test.ts` | Covers shapes, validation, legacy parser, completion version, and capability parsing. |
| `test/launch/guarded-control-never-follows-a-replacement.test.ts` | Covers new-ID replacement, same-ID generation increment, stale controls, pending wait, signal escalation, neighbor survival, and capability propagation; missing findings' concurrency/watcher cases. |
| `docs/tools/launch.md` | Documents user-facing pair, generation, capability probe and legacy fail-closed path; stronger blanket atomicity/retirement guarantees need qualification or implementation. |
| `packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md` | Declares behavior, pending above fixes. |
| `FEATURE_MAP.json` | Adds feature owner, coverage paths and test registry. |

### Consumer contract (accepted heylolo-evidence head bb9adecf)

Read [phone_driver.py at accepted head](https://github.com/Wladefant/heylolo-evidence/blob/bb9adecf7a5077a0919b105bcd0e87c87736acc9/phone-runs/2026-11-08-phonehunt2/phone_driver.py#L67-L135) and its [capability/start path](https://github.com/Wladefant/heylolo-evidence/blob/bb9adecf7a5077a0919b105bcd0e87c87736acc9/phone-runs/2026-11-08-phonehunt2/phone_driver.py#L274-L312). It requires exact `details.op`, `details.daemon.name/id/generation`, `list.details.capabilities.guardedIdentity === 1`, then guarded `send(text: "q") → wait(for: "exit") → stop` on escalation. The producer's **source interface** matches that contract, including `send` of `q\n` when Enter defaults true, and returns the generation in start/send/wait/stop snapshots. This is **source compatibility**, not proof of a live installed Windows broker, FFmpeg finalization, or the combined end-to-end recorder behavior. In particular, this PR does not establish exactly-once behavior across broker replacement.

### Verification provenance (do not conflate)

- **Producer-reported local source tests:** `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/launch/guarded-protocol.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/launch/guarded-control-never-follows-a-replacement.test.ts` — **29 pass, 0 fail, 107 expectations, 2 files**; recorded in PR body and [verification comment](https://github.com/Wladefant/veyyon/pull/1072#issuecomment-6732920705). These tests were **not independently executed in this review**.
- **Producer-reported scoped `tsgo`:** `tsgo -p tsconfig.scoped.json --noEmit` — **0 diagnostics**, focused changed scope. Whole-package check reportedly has **5 unclassified diagnostics** in `test/task/task-spawn-executor-cwd.test.ts`; **not** established as baseline.
- **CI seen through GitHub:** OVH CI associated with the exact head is **skipped**; no successful head-level CI status was available from the checked commit-status endpoint.
- **Installed/live:** unverified. No claim that a running broker reports `guardedIdentity:1`, that Windows PTY/stdin and native escalation work, or that accepted consumer PR #33 ran live against this producer revision.

**Final verdict: REQUEST CHANGES.** Fix the P1 retirement/replay race and the two P2 regressions, add the specified tests, rerun focused and scoped checks at the resulting exact head, and re-review. No code or tests were modified by this review.
